title: Presley Gerber’s Hollywood Hills Estate Listed for $3.6 Million After His Death【TMZ】
body:
Presley Gerber’s sleek Hollywood Hills residence has been listed for $3.6 million, just weeks after the 27‑year‑old model’s untimely death. The property, a modern two‑story home perched on a quiet cul‑de‑sac, is now on the market with a price tag that reflects both its prime location and the lingering public interest in Gerber’s legacy. Real‑estate agents say the listing is expected to draw considerable attention from buyers seeking a foothold in one of Los Angeles’ most coveted neighborhoods, as well as from fans and collectors hoping to own a piece of the late star’s story.

The 2,500‑square‑foot home, built in 2015, features floor‑to‑ceiling windows, a rooftop deck with panoramic city views, and a private garden that includes a small pool and a landscaped patio. Inside, the open‑plan living area flows into a gourmet kitchen equipped with high‑end appliances, while the second floor houses three bedrooms, including a master suite with a walk‑in closet and a spa‑like bathroom. According to the listing, recent upgrades include smart‑home technology, new hardwood flooring, and an energy‑efficient HVAC system, all of which contribute to the property’s elevated asking price.

Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford and former model and music executive Gerald Gerber, rose to prominence in the fashion world after signing with IMG Models in 2015. His career, though still in its early stages, featured runway appearances for major designers and a growing social‑media following that made him a staple of the celebrity‑influencer circuit. The sudden tragedy that claimed his life in early August—an apparent suicide—sent shockwaves through both the fashion industry and his extensive fan base. In the wake of his death, his family has been navigating legal and emotional complexities, including the disposition of his assets, of which the Hollywood Hills home is the most visible.

Industry insiders suggest that the decision to list the property so soon may be driven by a combination of practical and sentimental factors. “When a high‑profile estate becomes vacant, the market reacts quickly,” said a senior broker at a downtown LA firm who asked to remain anonymous. “There’s a surge of interest not only from investors but also from people who want to preserve a piece of cultural history.” The Gerber family’s representatives have not publicly commented on the timing, but the rapid move aligns with standard estate‑settlement practices, especially when the property is a primary residence that incurs ongoing maintenance costs.

The $3.6 million price point places the home within the mid‑range for comparable properties in the Hollywood Hills, where listings can swing from $2 million for modest condos to over $10 million for sprawling estates with extensive amenities. Analysts at a local real‑estate research firm note that the home’s unique selling proposition—its association with a well‑known figure—could either boost its desirability or deter traditional buyers wary of potential media scrutiny. “We’ve seen similar scenarios with celebrity homes; sometimes the fame adds a premium, other times it creates a niche market,” explained the firm’s senior analyst.

As the listing goes live, potential buyers will weigh the allure of owning a property tied to Gerber’s brief but impactful career against the practical considerations of price, location, and upkeep. The home’s imminent sale will also serve as a barometer for how the market values properties linked to recent tragedies, a delicate balance between respect for the deceased and the commercial realities of real estate. Regardless of the outcome, the sale will close a chapter on Gerger’s Los Angeles chapter, while his memory continues to resonate through fashion archives, social media tributes, and now, a property that may soon become someone else’s sanctuary.
